      "value": 0.59,

      "measures": "share of articles that stated the hypothesis or objective of the study, and the number and characteristics of the animals used",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting standards",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "articles",
      "verbatim": "The survey, commissioned by the National Centre for the Replacement, Refinement and Reduction of Animals in Research (NC3Rs), a UK Government-sponsored scientific organisation, found that only 59% of the 271 randomly chosen articles assessed stated the hypothesis or objective of the study, and the number and characteristics of the animals used (i.e., species/strain, sex, and age/weight)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "proportion of papers not reporting randomisation",
      "value": 0.87,
      "unit": "proportion",
      "measures": "share of papers that did not report using randomisation to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting standards",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "papers",
      "verbatim": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "proportion of papers not reporting blinding",
      "value": 0.86,
      "unit": "proportion",
      "measures": "share of papers that did not report using blinding to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting standards",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "papers",
      "verbatim": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "proportion of publications fully describing statistical methods",
      "value": 0.7,
      "unit": "proportion",
      "measures": "share of publications that used statistical methods and fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting standards",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "publications",
      "verbatim": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability [5]."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "proportion of articles not reporting the number of animals used",
      "value": 0.04,
      "unit": "proportion",
      "measures": "share of articles that did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting standards",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "journal articles",
      "verbatim": "Our review found that 4% of the 271 journal articles assessed did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections [5]."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and described the ARRIVE guidelines for reporting animal research to improve the quality and transparency of publications.",
  "what_it_found": "A review of published animal research found significant omissions in reporting, with only 59% of articles stating the hypothesis or objective and animal characteristics, and many failing to report randomisation, blinding, or statistical methods.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "The largest and most comprehensive review of published animal research undertaken to date, as far as we are aware, has highlighted serious omissions in the way research using animals is reported [5].",
      "topic": "Reporting Omissions"
    },
    {
      "quote": "only 59% of the 271 randomly chosen articles assessed stated the hypothesis or objective of the study, and the number and characteristics of the animals used (i.e., species/strain, sex, and age/weight).",
      "topic": "Key Reporting Deficiencies"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment.",
      "topic": "Bias Reduction Reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability [5].",
      "topic": "Statistical Reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "4% of the 271 journal articles assessed did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections [5].",
      "topic": "Animal Numbers"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Improved reporting of these and other details will maximise the availability and utility of the information gained from every animal and every experiment, preventing unnecessary animal use in the future.",
      "topic": "Reporting Benefits"
    }
  ]
